title: From Simulated Citizens to Simulated Deliberation: Challenges in Representation and Interaction
abstract: arXiv:2609.07573v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Multi-agent LLM deliberation has been explored as a scalable way to simulate public deliberation. For such simulations to be informative, persona agents should reflect population opinion patterns and interaction should shape their conclusions. We evaluate whether LLM-based deliberation can meet these two conditions using census-grounded Korean personas debating real policy questions benchmarked against national surveys. Persona agents do not reliably reproduce population opinion patterns: responses are often far more concentrated and frequently reverse demographic differences in the human data. Deliberations nonetheless produce reasoned, reciprocal, and varied arguments alongside substantial stance movement. Yet much of this movement does not require peer exchange: sealed-monologue agents change position at similar rates and reach nearly the same final balance as full debates, while groups initialized with very different positions often

translated_title: 从模拟公民到模拟审议：表征与互动中的挑战
translated_abstract: 多智能体大语言模型（LLM）审议已被探索为一种可扩展的模拟公共审议的方式。为了使此类模拟具有参考价值，角色智能体应能反映总体舆论模式，且互动应能塑造其结论。我们使用基于人口普查的韩国角色智能体就真实政策问题展开辩论，并以全国调查数据作为基准，评估基于LLM的审议能否满足这两个条件。结果显示，角色智能体并不能可靠地再现总体舆论模式：其回应往往远比人类数据更集中，且经常逆转人类数据中的人口统计学差异。尽管如此，审议过程仍然产生了有理有据、互惠且多样化的论证，并伴随着显著的立场转变。然而，这种立场转变的很大一部分并不依赖于同伴之间的交流：封闭式独白智能体以相似的速率改变立场，并达到与完整辩论几乎相同的最终立场平衡，而初始立场差异很大的群体往往……
tldr: 该研究评估了基于LLM的多智能体模拟公共审议的有效性，发现角色智能体无法可靠再现人口舆论模式，且审议中的立场转变大部分并不依赖智能体之间的互动交流。
en_tdlr: This study evaluates LLM-based multi-agent public deliberation simulation and finds that persona agents fail to reliably reproduce population opinion patterns, and much of the stance movement during deliberation does not require peer exchange.
